readerContract.humanQuestion: If an AI produces a correct mathematical result, why are leading mathematicians still worried?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Separate a correct answer from the slower work of explaining, attributing, teaching and building shared understanding.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No benchmark or mathematical-research vocabulary assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A benchmark can measure answer production without measuring whether a field can inspect, explain and build on the result.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A learner can receive a right answer without yet being able to explain the method or use it on a changed problem.
readerContract.surfaceJob: September 16 private Daily candidate about a collective professional response to AI mathematics benchmarks.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can use an AI answer while checking whether I learned a reusable method.

canonicalTruth.owner: The declaration signatories own the collective argument; Alessio Figalli owns his assessment; NewsStand owns bounded explanation.
canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Recheck the declaration and interview if publication slips after September 16 or either source changes materially.

candidateRepairPreflight.event: Collective declaration is the fresh event; the earlier Navier-Stokes claim is context only and not retold.
candidateRepairPreflight.attribution: Professional argument and one signatory assessment remain attributed.
candidateRepairPreflight.limits: No blanket empirical claim about what AI can understand, no consensus survey claim, and no causal education-harm claim.
candidateRepairPreflight.budget: All reader-visible source-derived wording, including source labels, stays within Le Monde 100 and ETH Zurich 200 words.

draftArchitecture.openingJob: Report the collective declaration and its answer-versus-understanding distinction.
causalSequence: A chosen benchmark rewards an observable result.
Mathematical work also includes inspection, attribution, explanation and transmission.
A learner tests understanding by explaining and transferring a method.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A percentage problem: receive an answer, hide it, explain the method and change one condition.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Ask what any benchmark measures and what work remains outside its score.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Use the two-pass explain-and-change check on one low-stakes problem.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No fictional character, race metaphor, repeated Navier-Stokes opening or claim about machine consciousness.

humourPlan.noneReason: Dry, restrained treatment keeps an unsettled professional argument clear.

readerQuestions.question: What did the collective declaration argue?
What does this evidence not establish?
Why can a correct answer differ from shared understanding?
How can a beginner test whether an answer became usable knowledge?

requiredTerms.meaning: a defined test used to compare performance on a chosen task

draftArchitecture.presentationPlan: Use the admitted people-free percentage notebook: exact 100 × 0.25 = 25 and one of four equal parts shaded. The image demonstrates an answer without claiming that the answer proves understanding.
draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: The declaration argues that fast correct results do not complete the field’s work of shared understanding.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Report the collective argument first; place evidence limits beside it; explain benchmark scope; finish with one low-stakes transfer check.

discoveryChecks.question: Does a correct AI answer prove that a learner understands the method?
discoveryChecks.answer: No; the learner can test transfer by explaining the method and solving a changed version.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Turning an attributed professional argument into an empirical claim that AI cannot understand.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Keep the declaration and Figalli assessment attributed, state evidence limits beside the report, and recount all reader-visible derived wording.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: Reader can distinguish a benchmark result from the broader work of understanding without receiving a blanket capability claim.
